setting.description: A remote lighthouse station in the early twentieth century.

attractors: The participant gathers evidence faster than any single explanation can absorb it, while a distinction they rely on quietly fails to hold.
invariants: The evidence stays consistent with more than one explanation for a long time, and some of it is noise.
No one the participant can reach knows the whole of what happened.
Making sense of the explanation the participant is building depends on a distinction that does not hold in this world.
Whatever bears on the explanation the participant is building follows this world's own customs, which make sense from inside and do not bend toward the participant's assumptions.
secrets: What happened has an ordinary cause and a significant consequence, and the two are easy to confuse.
